history.period: Modern (re-established after 1971); claims of 1000-year antiquity are local tradition and UNVERIFIED
history.summary: Matri Mandir, also called Ramna Kalibari, is a Goddess Kali temple at Polo-Lawmali near Police Bazar, Shillong (East Khasi Hills). Its identity is bound up with the original Ramna Kali Mandir on the outskirts of Dhaka, which was destroyed by the Pakistan Army on 27 March 1971 during the Bangladesh Liberation War; the Shillong temple is presented as its re-establishment in exile. Temple-promotional sources claim the shrine is a Swayambhu site as old as 1000 years, founded by a Nepalese-origin devotee of Kali and developed under Rani Bilashmoni Debi of the Bhawal estate, with a shikhara-style tower and a large sacred dighi (pond) - these antiquity claims are local tradition and UNVERIFIED, and the architecture visible today is modern. Contact number published by listings: 0364 222 7676 (verify). Opening hours conflict between sources (verify).

name: Matri Mandir (Ramna Kalibari)
town_description: Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya at about 1,525 m in the East Khasi Hills, is the former capital of undivided Assam, known as the 'Scotland of the East'. Its attractions include Shillong Peak, Elephant Falls, Wards Lake, the Don Bosco Museum and a vibrant music culture. Matri Mandir stands at Polo-Lawmali, about 1-1.5 km from Police Bazar, the city's main commercial hub.

travel.road: The temple is at Polo-Lawmali, easily reached by local taxi from Police Bazar and the main bus stand (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; visit 7:00-9:00 AM or 5:00-6:00 PM for a peaceful darshan. Photography is prohibited inside the sanctum (per bharattemples).
